newsitem.title: UK: Key UK by-election set for February 27 - minister.
newsitem.headline: Key UK by-election set for February 27 - minister.

text.p: The ruling Conservatives will later on Monday fire the starting gun for the crucial parliamentary by-election of Wirral South where polling will take place on February 27, Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell said.
"The by-election writ will be moved this afternoon and we are officially campaigning for February 27," he said during a visit to the Merseyside, north-west England constituency.
If Prime Minister John Major delays a general election until May 1, as he has indicated he wants to do, Wirral South will be the last major test of voter sentiment before the national contest.
On the other hand, if he opted for a March election, the Wirral battle might be called off.

Were the Conservatives to lose the seat, which they won by a majority of 8,183 votes at the 1992 general election, Major would head a minority government, with 322 Conservative MPs facing 323 from other parties in the House of Commons.
But Dorrell was upbeat about his party's chances of holding on despite national opinion polls putting them some 20 points behind the opposition Labour Party.
"The thing that will make this by-election different from other by-elections of this Parliament is that we are going to win it," he said.
However his optimism contrasted with the mood of Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine who said on Monday he expected Wirral South electors to use the by-election to "kick the government".

"There are a lot of people around who see by-elections as an opportunity to kick the Government and we would expect to see that," Heseltine said in London where he unveiled a new Conservative advertising poster attacking Labour's policies on Europe.
The Wirral by-election was caused by the death on November 3 of Conservative MP Barry Porter.
